solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Parrot about to stuff mouth (5)

indicatorNotes.to stuff: you stuff something by packing a filling inside it, so CA is packed into the mouth

blocks.note: a maw is an animal's mouth

annotation.surface: Someone feeds a talkative parrot, stuffing its mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: About sounds like a direction to go around; here it is the abbreviation for circa, and it is the filling, not the wrapper.
annotation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large long-tailed parrot of Central and South America, so parrot defines it by its family.

entries.clue: Romeo’s friend met Curio after tense exchanges with Romeo (8)

indicatorNotes.after: the letters of met Curio are taken as they stand once the swap has been made, so after sets the order of operations
indicatorNotes.exchanges with: to exchange places with someone is to swap positions, so T and R trade places

annotation.surface: A Shakespearean friend runs into a character called Curio, then trades barbs with Romeo.
annotation.walkthrough: In METCURIO the T and the R swap places. Curio is also a Shakespeare character, which helps the disguise, and Romeo does double duty on purpose.
annotation.definitionFit: Mercutio is Romeo's witty friend in Romeo and Juliet, so the definition names him by his role in the play.

entries.clue: Shell in vehicle shifting quickly (8)

annotation.surface: A shell rattles around inside a fast-moving vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: Shell could be petrol or ammunition here; it is the hard casing of a crab or tortoise.
annotation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle or crustacean, the zoologist's word for that shell.

entries.clue: Something covering features with a crude humourless act (6,9)

indicatorNotes.crude: something crude is roughly put together, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A disguise, a mask perhaps, worn for an unfunny, vulgar performance.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is W plus A plus HUMOURLESS ACT; crude sits in the middle of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick drooping one that hides the mouth, so it covers facial features.

entries.clue: Member of defence regularly saw what overlooked claims could be? (9)

blocks.note: a defender in football or rugby
to date someone is to see them regularly

annotation.surface: A defender kept an eye on something missed in a list of claims.
annotation.walkthrough: Regularly looks like an alternate-letters signal on saw; it is part of the phrase for going out with someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A claim that was overlooked might be backdated to the time it should have been paid.

entries.clue: Snubbed robust complaint (4)

indicatorNotes.Snubbed: a snub nose is short at the end, so snubbed means the last letter is cut

annotation.surface: A strong objection was brushed aside.
annotation.walkthrough: Snubbed reads as ignored; here it clips the tail of BEEFY.
annotation.definitionFit: Beef is informal slang for a grievance, as in what's your beef?

entries.clue: Meeting company with head lacking in deduction (10)

indicatorNotes.head lacking: the head of a word is its first letter, and it is missing

annotation.surface: A company meeting where the boss is not up to reasoning things out.
annotation.walkthrough: Head in a business surface suggests a chief; here it is the first letter of INFERENCE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a conference is a formal meeting for discussion.

entries.clue: Regional administrators instruct codicil should be changed (8,7)

indicatorNotes.should be changed: the letters are to be altered into a new order

annotation.surface: Local officials order that an addition to a will be amended.
annotation.walkthrough: A codicil is an addendum to a will, which gives the legal surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A district council is an elected body running a local area, so its members administer a region.

entries.clue: Warder missing northern country (6)

indicatorNotes.missing: a warder missing N is one without that letter, as a coat missing a button lacks it

blocks.note: an old word for a jailer

annotation.surface: A prison guard is absent from a country in the north.
annotation.walkthrough: A turnkey held the keys in an old prison.
annotation.definitionFit: Turkey is a country spanning Europe and Asia, defined by example.

entries.clue: Leave cornered, pulled up after partial loss of power (6)

indicatorNotes.pulled up: in a down answer, lifting it turns it the other way
indicatorNotes.partial loss of: only part of the letters for power, one P of two, go

annotation.surface: Someone trapped in a corner retreats after the electricity partly fails.
annotation.walkthrough: Reversing TRAPPED gives DEPPART, which has two Ps; losing one of them is the partial loss of power.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to depart is to leave, as trains depart a station.

entries.clue: Cleric managed to nab retiring journalist on Russian river (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to nab: to catch and hold, so the other pieces go inside
indicatorNotes.retiring: retiring means withdrawing, drawing back, so the journalist is read backwards

annotation.surface: A clergyman arrests a shy reporter beside a river in Russia.
annotation.walkthrough: Retiring reads as shy in the surface; it is the backwards signal. The journalist sits after the river, so on means placed next to.
annotation.definitionFit: A rural dean is a Church of England cleric overseeing a group of parishes.

entries.clue: Band splits after going west (5)

indicatorNotes.after going west: an across answer read westward runs right to left

annotation.surface: A pop group breaks up after moving west.
annotation.walkthrough: Band suggests musicians; it is a strip of material.
annotation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip of leather or fabric, the non-musical sense of band.

entries.clue: Reverse hype? Relax (6)

blocks.note: the prefix that undoes an action
a plug is a piece of publicity

annotation.surface: A plea to stop the hype and chill out.
annotation.walkthrough: Unplugging is taken as undoing a plug, with UN- doing the undoing.
annotation.definitionFit: Unplug is an informal idiom for switching off from work and unwinding.

entries.clue: This speaker approves two tries (4,4)

indicatorNotes.two: two tries means the word for tries is written twice

blocks.note: a judge hears, or tries, a case

annotation.surface: A speaker nods through a couple of attempts.
annotation.walkthrough: Tries means attempts in the surface; in court, to try a case is to hear it.
annotation.definitionFit: Hear hear is what a listener calls out in a debate to approve a point.

entries.clue: Duke’s gushing, not upset (10)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down answer, turned upside down reverses it

annotation.surface: A duke is effusive but not upset.
annotation.walkthrough: Duke’s means Duke is; upset reads as unhappy but turns NOT over.
annotation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo, so the title alone points to him.

entries.clue: Corrupt eminent cop; extremely cocky example of uselessness (12)

indicatorNotes.Corrupt: something corrupted is spoiled, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, the first and last letters

annotation.surface: A senior officer on the take, and arrogant with it, is hopeless.
annotation.walkthrough: Only EMINENT COP is rearranged; CY is added at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Incompetency is the state of being useless at a job, so any instance of it is an example of uselessness.

entries.clue: Naval location cut short, over 0.9144m (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down answer, the first piece sits above the next

blocks.note: to dock a tail is to cut it short

annotation.surface: A naval site cut back by just under a metre.
annotation.walkthrough: The odd number is simply a yard in metric.
annotation.definitionFit: A dockyard is where naval ships are built and repaired, defined by where it is found.

entries.clue: Lloyd set fancy typeface (3,5)

indicatorNotes.fancy: elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A man named Lloyd chose an ornate font.
annotation.walkthrough: Set belongs to the fodder, though it looks like a typesetting word.
annotation.definitionFit: Old Style is a family of serif typefaces.

entries.clue: Local left in charge of small hospital in trendy teaching institution (6,6)

indicatorNotes.in: hospital in trendy means the H is placed inside the word for trendy

blocks.note: the local is your nearest pub

annotation.surface: The pub left a small hospital in charge of a fashionable college.
annotation.walkthrough: The local is British for your usual pub. A British public school is, confusingly, a private fee-paying school.
annotation.definitionFit: A public school in Britain is an independent fee-paying school, a kind of teaching institution.

entries.clue: Shocked judge took flight having lost billions (6)

indicatorNotes.having lost: something that has lost a letter no longer has it, so B is dropped

annotation.surface: A judge ran off in alarm after losing billions.
annotation.walkthrough: B for billions comes off BOLTED; the surface makes it sound like a financial scandal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to be jolted is to be given a sudden shock.

entries.clue: Arm functioning after electronic hand shackles withdrawn (6)

indicatorNotes.shackles: to shackle is to hold captive, so the hand holds E inside
indicatorNotes.after: functioning comes after the rest in the answer

blocks.note: a paw is a hand, reversed to WAP

annotation.surface: A limb working again after an electronic tag on the hand is taken off.
annotation.walkthrough: Arm reads as a limb in the surface; it is a noun meaning a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, as in the arms trade, so one arm is one weapon.

entries.clue: Deliberate individual nuance (8)

annotation.surface: A pondering of a person's subtle shade of meaning.
annotation.walkthrough: Deliberate reads as a verb, to ponder; it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: An overtone is a subtle additional sense, the same shade of meaning as a nuance.

entries.clue: Shakes “a kilo” in brief search (6)

indicatorNotes.in: a kilo in the search means those letters sit inside it
indicatorNotes.brief: a brief thing is cut short, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A quick hunt turns up a quivering kilo of something.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks just bundle a kilo as one piece; K is the kilo abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something that quakes shakes or trembles.

entries.clue: A round American fruit (4)

indicatorNotes.round: to go round something is to surround it

blocks.note: as in ten pounds a head, per head

annotation.surface: A round fruit from America.
annotation.walkthrough: A looks like the letter A; it is PER, which wraps round A for American.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: pears are an orchard crop grown for eating, one kind among many.

entries.clue: Matter of huge imaginary circle having radius cut (5)

indicatorNotes.cut: having the radius cut means it is taken out of the circle

blocks.note: a line of latitude round the globe
the r of geometry formulas, removed

annotation.surface: A geometry question about a vast circle with a shortened radius.
annotation.walkthrough: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are imaginary circles round the Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the topic is the subject matter under discussion.

entries.clue: Article, risqué, about old Conservative form of government (9)

annotation.surface: A saucy newspaper piece about a Tory government of the past.
annotation.walkthrough: About only means concerning here: RACY comes after the O and C it is about.
annotation.definitionFit: Theocracy is government by priests in the name of God, one form of government among many.

entries.clue: Screw undone, ergo nearly out (9)

indicatorNotes.nearly: not quite all, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.out: put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A loose screw, so it must be almost out.
annotation.walkthrough: Screw is British slang for a prison warder, which a dungeoner is.
annotation.definitionFit: A dungeoner is a jailer, and screw is slang for a prison officer.

entries.clue: Organ essentially protected by vein implant (5)

indicatorNotes.essentially: at its essence, the middle letter

annotation.surface: A heart or kidney is carefully stitched into a vein during a transplant.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is surgical, but vein is a seam of ore and implant is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To lodge something is to fix it firmly in place, the same sense as implanting it.
